代.meaning: When the <part>coat hook</part> bends under a soaking wet coat, you hammer a wooden <part>stake</part> into the wall beside it and hang the coat there instead. It's not a real hook, but it works. It's a <kanji>substitute</kanji>.
代.on: You roll a pair of <sound>di</sound>ce to decide which one gets your hat.
代.kun: Next morning a wet <sound>ca</sound>rp is hanging on the stake in place of your coat.

寝.meaning: Under the <part>roof</part>, a farmer leans his <part>climbing pole</part> and his <part>rake</part> against the wall, pulls a <part>blanket</part> over his head and twists into a <part>pretzel</part> on the floor, boots still on. He's done for the day. Time to <kanji>lie down</kanji>.
寝.on: He kicks off one boot in his sleep, and it bangs him on the <sound>shin</sound>.
寝.kun: Snoring, he tugs the blanket up to his <sound>ne</sound>ck.

試.meaning: Before the big <part>ceremony</part>, the mayor practises his <part>speech</part> to an empty hall. Mic on: one, two, one, two. Does it echo? Does anyone laugh at the jokes? It's only a <kanji>test</kanji>.
試.on: A knight in the back row holds up a <sound>shi</sound>eld with a score painted on it: four out of ten.
試.kun: The trial audience is a <sound>ko</sound>ala, a <sound>co</sound>conut and a <sound>ro</sound>dent, and only the coconut doesn't laugh.

服.meaning: Under the <part>moon</part>, a tailor sews all night. He twists each sleeve into a <part>pretzel</part> fold, and when the cloth won't lie flat, he presses it down with the heavy handle of a rubber <part>stamp</part>, like a tiny iron. By morning the shop is full of <kanji>clothing</kanji>.
服.on: Every shirt goes up on a big <sound>hook</sound> by the door, ready to be sold.

甘.meaning: Two posts poke up through a long bar, with a short bar held between them like a sugar cube on a tongue. The cube melts, the tongue curls, and your whole face smiles. It tastes <kanji>sweet</kanji>.
甘.on: A bee buzzes out of a pink <sound>carn</sound>ation, carrying a drop of honey.
甘.kun: You lick the honey: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' Then you run to your <sound>Ma</sound> to ask for more.

案.meaning: You <part>relax</part> in a hammock tied to a <part>tree</part>, eyes half shut. Then an idea drops on you like an acorn: a treehouse! Ladders, ropes, a slide. Before you've even sat up, you have a <kanji>plan</kanji>.
案.on: Your <sound>un</sound>cle reads it, nods, and goes to fetch his saw.
案.kun: You spread the plans out, sneeze '<sound>Tsu</sound>!', and a <sound>cu</sound>ckoo and its <sound>e</sound>gg roll off the wooden top: a desk.

冬.meaning: Someone leaves a <part>folding chair</part> out on the porch, and by morning two chips of <part>ice</part> hang under its seat. The pond is frozen, the trees are bare, and nobody will sit outside for months. It's <kanji>winter</kanji>.
冬.on: You step out barefoot and stub your frozen <sound>toe</sound> on the chair.
冬.kun: Back inside, you hide under your <sound>fu</sound>ton and strum a sad song on your <sound>u</sound>kulele.

建.meaning: A painter dips a giant <part>brush</part> in wet cement and crosses an empty lot with one <part>long stride</part> after another, painting walls straight up out of the ground. By sunset there's a whole house. That's how he likes to <kanji>build</kanji>.
建.on: He starts small: first he paints a <sound>ken</sound>nel for his dog.
建.kun: Then he paints a stall for his <sound>ta</sound>co truck right next door.

英.meaning: In the <part>center</part> of a wet green lawn of <part>grass</part>, someone sets out a table with a teapot, scones and a tiny flag, and it starts to drizzle. Nobody moves. They just sip their tea. This must be <kanji>England</kanji>.
英.on: A squirrel under the table nibbles an <sound>a</sound>corn, staying perfectly polite.
英.kun: '<sound>Ha</sound>!' The squirrel tucks a <sound>na</sound>an, a toy <sound>bu</sound>ll and a <sound>sa</sound>rdine into a bunch of blossoms: a flower cluster.

化.meaning: You hang a <part>spoon</part> on the <part>coat hook</part> overnight. In the morning it's a fork. The next day it's a ladle, then a tiny umbrella. Whatever you hang there won't stay the same: everything starts to <kanji>change</kanji>.
化.on: On day four it turns into a <sound>ca</sound>rp and flops onto the floor.
化.kun: On day five the carp turns into a sheep, which gives one short '<sound>Ba</sound>!'

若.meaning: A sprout of <part>grass</part> pokes up out of the soil, and you lift it gently in your <part>right</part> hand. It's pale green, soft, barely a day old. It hasn't had time to grow up yet: it's <kanji>young</kanji>.
若.on: You plant it in the warm steam beside a bubbling <sound>jacu</sound>zzi so it grows faster.
若.kun: '<sound>Wah</sound>!' the sprout wails like a baby, so you rock it beside a <sound>ca</sound>rp pond until it sleeps.

盛.meaning: You put a single grape on a <part>dish</part>, and it starts to <part>turn into</part> more: two grapes, ten, a pile, a mountain spilling over the edge onto the floor. Your shop can't sell them fast enough. It's a <kanji>boom</kanji>.
盛.on: You lock the takings in a steel <sound>sa</sound>fe, and soon that won't shut either.
盛.kun: A customer asks for a little, and you heap her plate so high that grapes roll into her <sound>mo</sound>ccasin: to pile on.

革.meaning: A cow's hide is stretched flat to dry: a <part>goal</part>-shaped rack holds the top, a <part>mouth</part>-shaped frame holds the middle, and a <part>ten</part>-shaped peg pins the tail. Once it's dry and tough, the hide is <kanji>leather</kanji>.
革.on: A crow pecks at the old <sound>carc</sound>ass nearby, but the leather is far too tough for its beak.
革.kun: A <sound>ca</sound>rp flops onto the drying hide and slides right off with a '<sound>Wah</sound>!'

靴.meaning: A cobbler takes a sheet of <part>leather</part>, folds it and taps it, and it starts to <part>change</part>: a toe, a heel, laces. Two of them hop off the bench and stand side by side. A new pair of <kanji>shoes</kanji>.
靴.on: The first customer is a <sound>ca</sound>rp, who has nowhere to put them.
靴.kun: A <sound>cu</sound>ckoo pops out of the left shoe and sneezes: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!'

息.meaning: You sprint across town to a <part>phone booth</part>, squeeze in and slam the door. Your <part>heart</part> pounds, the glass fogs up, and you're puffing too hard to say hello. All you can do is catch your <kanji>breath</kanji>.
息.on: You wipe the foggy glass clean with a smelly <sound>sock</sound>.
息.kun: You fish a wriggling <sound>ee</sound>l and a brass <sound>key</sound> out of your pocket, and breathe on the key until it shines.

春.meaning: The old <part>Christmas tree</part> is still in the garden, and now the <part>sun</part> shines warm right under it. Its needles turn green again, buds pop out, and birds start building nests in it. It's <kanji>springtime</kanji>.
春.on: You drag out a garden chair and a fat cu<sound>shion</sound> to sit under it in the warm air.
春.kun: '<sound>Ha</sound>!' you laugh, as a <sound>roo</sound>k drops a twig on your head for its nest.

昨.meaning: The <part>sun</part> sets behind the <part>coat rack</part> in the hall, where your coat from the day before still hangs, crumpled, its pockets full of old receipts. You meant to wash it. That was <kanji>yesterday</kanji>.
昨.on: On the shelf beside it, a fat <sound>suc</sound>culent you forgot to water is still waiting.

族.meaning: A boat with a big <part>sail</part> drifts up to an island, and from a <part>diving board</part> on the cliff, people leap into the sea to meet it, each with a <part>dart</part> tucked behind one ear. Grandparents, kids, cousins: one dart, one <kanji>tribe</kanji>.
族.on: Each child has a <sound>zo</sound>diac sign painted on one cheek and a <sound>cu</sound>ckoo feather in its hair.

供.meaning: The whole class hangs its homework on the <part>coat hook</part> by the door, then, all <part>together</part>, lifts the bundle onto the teacher's desk. It's done, it's in, no more changes. They <kanji>submit</kanji> it.
供.on: The teacher locks the pile in a drawer with a brass <sound>key</sound>, and the whole class lets out one long, relieved '<sound>Ohhh</sound>!'
供.kun: Then they offer the teacher a <sound>so</sound>fa to rest on and a warm <sound>na</sound>an.

渡.meaning: A ferry sloshes through the <part>water drops</part> of a cold river while the captain checks his compass, turning a few <part>degrees</part> left, then right. Cars, bikes and goats ride on his deck. The whole trip is one long <kanji>transit</kanji>.
渡.on: On the far bank, the passengers tie the ferry up to a <sound>to</sound>tem pole.
渡.kun: '<sound>Wah</sound>!' squeals a goat as a wave splashes the deck and knocks a <sound>ta</sound>co out of its mouth.

察.meaning: Under the temple <part>roof</part>, a priest begins a strange <part>ritual</part>: he shakes a bowl, drops a pebble and squints at where it lands. Will it rain tomorrow? Will the cat come home? He doesn't know. He can only <kanji>guess</kanji>.
察.on: This time he squints at the peel of a <sound>sats</sound>uma and guesses: sunny.

警.meaning: A teacher stands so tall that the whole class goes quiet in <part>awe</part>. Then comes the <part>speech</part>: no running, no shouting, no gum under the desks. Fingers wag, eyebrows rise. She is about to <kanji>admonish</kanji> them.
警.on: One kid hides a slice of birthday <sound>ca</sound>ke under his desk, and gets told off for that too.
警.kun: '<sound>Ee</sound>!' squeals the kid. '<sound>Ma</sound>, she's telling off my <sound>shee</sound>p as well!'

告.meaning: A <part>cow</part> lifts its head over the fence, opens its <part>mouth</part>, and instead of mooing says in plain words: 'The grass really is greener over there.' The farmer drops his bucket. It's a <kanji>revelation</kanji>.
告.on: A <sound>coc</sound>katoo on the fence repeats the news to the whole farm.
告.kun: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' the cow sneezes, then tells the farmer the weather.

官.meaning: Under a grand <part>roof</part>, a man sits behind a <part>pole</part>-straight stack of forms, and his <part>mouth</part> opens and shuts on just three words: 'Wrong form, next!' He stamps, he sighs, he sends you away. He's a <kanji>bureaucrat</kanji>.
官.on: He only cheers up when someone hands him a pink <sound>carn</sound>ation for his buttonhole.

充.meaning: Mum lifts the <part>lid</part> off the cookie jar and counts out exactly three each. The <part>toddler</part> holds out both hands for more. 'Three,' says Mum, firmly. Everyone gets the same share: that's how you <kanji>allot</kanji>.
充.on: The toddler hides one cookie in a <sound>jew</sound>el box for later.
充.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' says Mum when she finds it, and that cookie counts as tomorrow's share.

越.meaning: A <part>runner</part> races to the edge of a <part>cliff</part>, plants a <part>spear</part> like a vaulting pole and flies clean over the gap, past every rival stuck at the edge. Nobody has ever jumped that far. She will <kanji>surpass</kanji> them all.
越.on: On the far side, someone has already made an <sound>etch</sound>ing of her jump on a metal plate.
越.kun: She lands right next to a sleepy <sound>ko</sound>ala, who doesn't even look up.

竹.meaning: Two green stalks shoot up side by side, each with a little <part>diving board</part> leaf at the top. Frogs climb up and dive off into the pond below: plop, plop. The stalks are tall and hollow: <kanji>bamboo</kanji>.
竹.on: A panda sits beneath it munching a <sound>chick</sound>pea instead of bamboo, for a change.
竹.kun: The panda stuffs a <sound>ta</sound>co with bamboo shoots and puts the <sound>ke</sound>ttle on for tea.

箸.meaning: <part>Someone</part> at the noodle bar snaps two thin sticks off a stalk of <part>bamboo</part>, clicks them together and pinches up a single grain of rice. Click, click, slurp. A pair of <kanji>chopsticks</kanji>.
箸.on: Above the bar, a <sound>cho</sound>pper hovers, dropping noodles from the sky.
箸.kun: '<sound>Ha</sound>!' he laughs, catching a falling noodle and feeding it to a <sound>shee</sound>p.

達.meaning: A <part>sheep</part> stands on a pile of <part>soil</part> at the foot of a steep <part>ramp</part>, takes a deep breath and charges up it, all the way to the top without slipping once. The other sheep bleat in wonder. She's an <kanji>accomplished</kanji> climber.
達.on: At the top she's handed a <sound>ta</sound>co, sneezes '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' and sprays it everywhere.
達.kun: Up come her friends, a <sound>ta</sound>co seller and a <sound>chee</sound>tah, and they all pose for the photo: the whole gang.

営.meaning: <part>Fireworks</part> burst over the night market. Under a <part>blanket</part> tent, the owner sits with a straight <part>spine</part> at her table, counting stalls, coins and helpers and keeping everyone in line. She knows how to <kanji>manage</kanji>.
営.on: She pays each helper one shiny <sound>a</sound>corn a day, and nobody complains.
営.kun: '<sound>Ee</sound>!' she squeaks, as a <sound>to</sound>tem pole topples onto a stall of <sound>na</sound>an.
